what: D1. Each dispatcher tick, admitIntakeSurfaceParts reads in one statement every kept surface with no part queued: whether it has a planned part, the case's frame, context, site and archived flag, and the distinct pins (caseContextSha256, accessSha256, readerSha256) of its published parts' jobs. An item is due when it has a planned part or a published part whose pins differ from the case's current pins (the context the readers fingerprint, the local access and the reader hash). At most one page of items, oldest first.

In the item's transaction, after the reader's source authority and the same admission lock as the first admission, one statement takes the lowest part that is planned, or published from a job whose pins differ from the current ones (only while the source is the latest revision). That part is enrolled with the same stable-id rule under the current pin, inside the reader's caps; a busy reader leaves it as it is.

D2. Nothing is deleted: the old job, its result and its artifact stay. The part row shows queued with the new job id until the reader accepts it; the accepted result then names the earlier job ids in result_ref.earlier. The parts list shows no result hash while a part is not published. A display read of a part being read again (not published, with an earlier result) returns today's 409 words: 'This part was read under an older batch context, so it is not shown as current.'

D3. A file waiting for its area (waitsForAreaTx) is not read again until the area binds. A read again that fails rests quarantined with the reader's code in the item's words and is never offered again.

D4. The first part read again under a pin marks every part read elsewhere and stores the count in plan_ref.reread; while any marked part is not yet read again the item is 'reading' and its words begin 'Read again under the batch's area: <n> of <m> parts.'

If the context comes back to an earlier pin before a read again ends, the part's accepted read under that pin is current again (published with its own job) and the count is taken again under that pin, so no part waits on a job that has already ended.
